title: "{{< fa gavel >}} Policies"

This syllabus and the dates are subject to change.

## Class

This class is meant to be *hands on*. You are responsible for the assigned
reading before each class. Please bring a charged laptop.

## Attendance

If you feel unwell please do not come to class. All class material is posted, and
I am happy to meet outside class to help you catch up.

## Computing

We use Python in Google Colab, so there is nothing to install. See
[Getting Started with Colab](colab.qmd).

## Course components

### Application exercises

Done in class, in pairs or small groups.

### Problem sets

Due Fridays. 

You may work together, however I want you to write up your own answers. If you work with other classmates please note that on your problem set. Graded for completion.

### Check-ins

Most weeks we will have one check-in at the start of class. They will typically cover topics similar to the problem sets.


### Exams

We will have two midterm exams and a final exam. Exams will be in class and closed book. 

## Grading

| Component | Weight |
|---|---|
| Problem sets | 5% |
| Check-ins | 20% |
| Midterm 1 | 25% |
| Midterm 2 | 25% |
| Final Exam | 25% |
| **Total** | **100%** |

| Letter | Numeric |
|---|---|
| A | > 94 |
| A- | 90 to 94 |
| B+ | 87 to 89 |
| B | 83 to 86 |
| B- | 80 to 82 |
| C+ | 77 to 79 |
| C | 73 to 76 |
| C- | 70 to 72 |
| D+ | 67 to 69 |
| D | 65 to 66 |
| F | Below 65 |

## Late and missed work

- Problem sets, late but within 24 hours of the due time: 50% credit  
- Any later: no credit  


All regrade requests must be raised with me within one week of receiving the
grade.

## Accessibility

Academic accommodations are coordinated through the Center for
Learning, Access, and Student Success (CLASS). If you would like to request
accommodations for this course, contact CLASS as early in the semester as
possible (class.wfu.edu, 118 Reynolda Hall).

## Honor code

Wake Forest University is committed to a culture of academic integrity. As a part
of this community, you share the responsibility for creating a place of honesty,
intellectual curiosity, and individual accountability. As you committed to with
your honor pledge signature, you agree "not to deceive any member of the
community; not to steal, cheat, or plagiarize on academic work; and not to engage
in any other form of academic misconduct." If you have questions about
documenting your work, working with external sources, or working with peers on
assigned work, consult with me as soon as possible. Instances of academic
dishonesty will be referred to the Honor and Ethics Council.

### Sharing code and responses

On **problem sets** you may use online resources, including StackOverflow and AI
assistants, and you **must cite** any borrowed or adapted code, whether copied
directly or modified. Un-cited reuse is treated as plagiarism.

Check-ins and exams are closed book and closed device.

## Getting help

See the [Help](help.qmd) page for office hours, the Math & Stats Center.
